title: Customer Migration Readiness Scorecard and Action Playbook
author: Nina Kaur
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable readiness scorecard and associated action playbooks to evaluate enterprise customers prior to major migrations (model upgrades, Dedicated tenant cutovers, Private deployment go-lives). It turns qualitative readiness discussions into a quantified pass/fail state and prescribes concrete remediation steps for each risk tier.

Scope: Applies to any enterprise migration where the customer will experience user-visible behavior changes or infrastructure cutovers. Not intended for trivial config flips.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
- Pre-cutover health review (recommended 14 days before migration).
- Canary-to-production transition decision (after canary window).
- Escalation input for QBRs when planning major changes.

Success criteria
----------------
- Readiness score >= 85% => Green: proceed with standard cutover.
- Readiness score 65%–84% => Amber: require mitigation plan and extended monitoring window before cutover.
- Readiness score < 65% => Red: block cutover until corrective actions completed and re-evaluated.

Scorecard structure (summary table)
----------------------------------
Each category is scored 0–10. We compute a weighted score. Weighted categories and target thresholds are in the table below.

| Category                         | Weight | Acceptable threshold (Green)        | Evidence required (examples) |
|----------------------------------|--------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Telemetry & Observability        | 0.25   | Full coverage, P50/P95 dashboards   | Dashboards, queries, synthetic tests |
| Stability & Synthetic Validation | 0.20   | No silent degradations in 72h       | Synthetic job history, alert history |
| Security & Compliance            | 0.15   | All gates passed (SSO, KMS, audit) | Audit logs, SAML test, KMS access test |
| Performance & Latency            | 0.15   | P95 latency within SLA              | Perf benchmark results, profiled traces |
| Cost & Quota                     | 0.10   | Cost guardrails, quota presets in place | Billing preview, quota config screenshots |
| Operational Runbooks & Staffing  | 0.10   | On-call documented and trained      | Runbook links, oncall roster, tabletop notes |
| Stakeholder Alignment & Signoff  | 0.05   | Executive and technical signoff     | Signed email / ticket approvals |

Scoring rubric
--------------
1. For each category assign 0–10 points using the guidance in the Evidence required column.
2. Multiply by the weight and sum to produce a final percent score (0–100).
3. Document the subjective risk notes for each category.

Example scoring calculation (short):
- Telemetry: 8/10 * 0.25 = 2.0
- Stability: 6/10 * 0.20 = 1.2
- Security: 9/10 * 0.15 = 1.35
- Performance: 8/10 * 0.15 = 1.2
- Cost: 7/10 * 0.10 = 0.7
- Runbooks: 6/10 * 0.10 = 0.6
- Stakeholders: 10/10 * 0.05 = 0.5
Total = 7.55 -> 75.5% => Amber.

Detailed category checks and remediation playbooks
------------------------------------------------
Telemetry & Observability (owner: CS-observability-engineer)
- Required checks:
  - P50/P95 latency dashboard exists for affected routes and models.
  - Error-rate, 4xx/5xx, and tokenized-error events tracked.
  - Synthetic journeys (happy path + two edge cases) running every 5 minutes with alerting.
  - Correlation between request_id and customer_request_id in traces.
- Telemetry assertions (examples you can copy):
  - avg(request_latency_ms{tenant=\"ACME\"}[15m]) < 200
  - increase(rate(error_count_total{tenant=\"ACME\"}[10m])) < 3x baseline
  - synthetic_success_rate{scenario=\"invoice_parse\"} > 0.99 over 24h
- Remediation steps (Amber):
  1. Instrument missing metrics using the ingestion helper: curl -X POST $OBS_INGEST_URL -d '{"metric": "synthetic_success", "tenant": "ACME"}'
  2. Add quick dashboards via template: /dashboards/templates/latency-tenant-template -> copy + update tenant filter.
  3. Re-run synthetic suite and wait 24 hours before re-score.

Stability & Synthetic Validation (owner: CS-reliability-lead)
- Required checks:
  - No silent degradation in last 72 hours (trend-based detection).
  - Canary tests exercised with production-like payloads for min 48 hours.
  - No surge-induced queueing or token-throttles in logs.
- Canary validation checklist (executable):
  1. Seed canary traffic at 1% of production for 24h, then 5% for 24h.
  2. Compare model output quality on guarded prompts (sample set of 250 prompts); flag regression > 2% by eval harness.
  3. Verify KV-cache hit-rate remains within 10% of baseline.
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Reduce canary traffic and extend observation window; introduce gradual route weight increase script.
  - If output-quality regression observed: revert candidate model to previous model for canary and open model-quality ticket.

Security & Compliance (owner: Security-Integrations)
- Required checks:
  - SSO/SAML authentication end-to-end test signed off.
  - KMS/HSM integration tested for key unwrap on sample workloads.
  - Audit logging enabled for all tenant-sensitive endpoints.
- Evidence examples:
  - SAML assertion capture screenshot.
  - KMS access logs showing UnwrapKey actions for tenant.
- Remediation (Red/Amber):
  1. Block cutover if KMS tests fail or if audit logging is incomplete.
  2. Run security dry-run with Security-Integrations team and re-check.

Performance & Latency (owner: Platform-performance)
- Required checks:
  - P50 and P95 latencies measured under production-shaped synthetic load.
  - Memory and GPU utilization profiles during load test captured.
  - SLOs: P95 < 600ms for interactive routes; batch routes P95 < 1200ms (customize per customer SLA).
- Load test commands (example):
  - ./loadgen --target-endpoint https://api.redwood.example/tenant/ACME/generate --concurrency 50 --duration 30m --payload-file samples.json
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Tune batching and concurrency knobs; update autoscaler target from 70%->60% if resource pressure observed.
  - Consider temporary capacity bump (Dedicated burst) for cutover window.

Cost & Quota (owner: CS-finops)
- Required checks:
  - Billing-preview run for projected model consumption for 14 days post-cutover.
  - Quota & rate-limit presets aligned with customer's SLAs and cost-guardrails.
- Evidence examples:
  - Billing preview CSV attached to migration ticket.
  - Quota config screenshot from tenant admin.
- Remediation (Amber):
  - Apply conservative rate limits or token caps for first 72 hours.
  - Enable automated quota alerts to oncall and CS-finops.

Operational Runbooks & Staffing (owner: CS-ops)
- Required checks:
  - Runbooks linked in migration ticket for rollback, failback, and incident triage.
  - On-call rotation and primary/secondary names listed with pager numbers.
  - Tabletop tabletop noted (one simulated cutover rehearsal within 7 days).
- Runbook checklist snippet:
  1. Rollback command set: tenant_switch --tenant ACME --model old-model-id --force
  2. Diagnostic bundle collection: /scripts/collect-tenant-bundle.sh ACME -> artifact uploaded to ticket.
  3. Customer communication templates present and approved.

Stakeholder Alignment & Signoff
------------------------------
- Required signoffs: Technical lead (customer), Technical lead (Redwood CS/Platform), Security approver (if private/delegated), Commercial approver for any temporary pricing changes.
- Signoff template (copy into ticket):
  - Technical lead (customer): [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Redwood platform lead: [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Security: [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK
  - Finance (if applicable): [name] - APPROVED / NEEDS_WORK

Automated gating and CI enforcement
----------------------------------
- We integrate the scorecard into the migration ticket workflow via a checklist macro. If score < 65% the ticket status auto-blocks through the CI rule: migration_gate :fail. If Amber (65–84%) the migration_gate returns soft-block with required mitigation checklist attached.
- Implementation note for engineers: the migration checker reads a YAML artifact stored in the ticket as follows: 
  - readiness_score: 75
  - blockers: ["canary_quality_regression"]
  - owner: "CS-reliability-lead"

Cutover runbook (high level)
---------------------------
1. Pre-cutover (T-48h): final smoke synthetic run, verify dashboards, confirm on-call.
2. Pre-cutover (T-2h): freeze config changes, create final snapshot of model config and KV cache metadata.
3. Cutover (T0): route weight shift in 3 steps: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with validation windows (10m, 20m, 30m).
4. Observe (T0 + 0–24h): telemetry assertions monitored; pager escalation on any P95 regression > 20% or error_rate spike > 0.5%.
5. Post-cutover (T+24–72h): cost preview re-run and customer QBR notification for final signoff.

Rollback criteria (must be explicit)
-----------------------------------
Trigger an automatic rollback if any of the following happen within the first 24 hours after reaching 100%:
- P95 latency increases > 2x baseline and absolute P95 > SLA threshold.
- Error rate (5xx) increases > 0.5% absolute and sustained for 10m.
- Synthetic success rate drops below 97% for the primary scenario over 30m.
- Customer visible quality regression flagged by their technical lead and reproduced by CS QA.

Escalation matrix (contact order)
--------------------------------
1. On-call Engineer (Platform) — 15 minutes to acknowledge.
2. CS Reliability Lead — 30 minutes to engage with customer.
3. Product/Model Owner — 60 minutes to provide root cause guidance.
4. Security — immediate if any PII/data-access concerns.
5. Executive on-call — for degraded SLA incidents longer than 4 hours.

Post-mortem and QBR integration
-------------------------------
- For any cutover that required rollback or produced an incident with customer impact, create a 72-hour incident summary and a 30-day technical retro. Feed outcomes into the next customer QBR: include readiness score history, mitigations performed, and updated risk posture.

Appendix: Example queries, commands, and artifacts
--------------------------------------------------
- Synthetic run command (example):
  - curl -X POST https://ci.redwood.example/synthetics/run -d '{"tenant":"ACME","suite":"invoice_parse","duration_minutes":60}'
- Example PromQL snippets:
  - p95_latency_ms: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{tenant=\"ACME\"}[5m])) by (le))
  - error_rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"ACME\", status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=\"ACME\"}[5m]))
- Templates and artifacts to attach to a migration ticket:
  - billing-preview.csv
  - synthetic-summary-<date>.json
  - runbook-links.txt
  - signed-approvals.pdf
